stages.title: A small surface fire
stages.description: A localized ignition starts the story above organic ground.
stages.evidence: Flames are a visual cue. The field view shows the numerical temperature state.

stages.title: The fire moves underground
stages.description: The story illustrates a buried peat fire. A moving underground front is not resolved by this calculation.
stages.evidence: Underground spread is prescribed in the natural story. Accepted numerical fields show heating and oxidation without a resolved moving subsurface front.

stages.title: Drill and open a buried pocket
stages.description: At 70% illustrated peat involvement, a tracked excavator arrives, drills the shaft, opens a wider buried pocket with a folding cutter, then withdraws.
stages.evidence: Drilling, excavation and displaced cuttings are staged; not a solved excavation model.

stages.title: Lower the dry ice
stages.description: A finite dry-ice sphere enters the open borehole after the drill is removed.
stages.evidence: Placement is prescribed. Natural-view source mass follows the separate finite contact-model inventory; accepted experiment inventory is reported separately.

stages.title: A buried inverted plate
stages.description: A folded segmented steel shell passes through the shaft and opens into the illustrated buried pocket above the dry ice.
stages.evidence: Folding, underreaming, deployment and wedge engagement are authored mechanisms, not a tool design or failure prediction.

stages.title: A rapid pressure release
stages.description: Rapid mode illustrates a pressure burst, ground uplift and plate inversion. Gradual mode retains its finite contact-model source.
stages.evidence: Ground rupture and plate inversion are prescribed visual events. CO₂ is nonflammable; no detonation or rupture pressure is calculated.

stages.title: Water follows assumed paths
stages.description: A woven fabric hose feeds the borehole; nearby cracks and soil darken gradually as a limited wetting front advances.
stages.evidence: Paths and wetting rates are assumed. Local contact cooling has a separate finite mass/energy budget; infiltration and treatment success are not predicted.

stages.title: Inspect what remains
stages.description: Some peat can remain hot. Compare the visual narrative with the available solver evidence.
stages.evidence: This is not a validated treatment procedure or a prediction of extinguishment.
